This landmark regional event explores the intersections of art and science, both past and present. PST ART is a Getty Initiative. The carbon emissions from this exhibition have been measured and reduced as a part of MOCA’s climate commitment. Support provided by the MOCA Environmental Council. Olafur Eliasson: OPEN is organized by José Luis Blondet, Senior Curator, and Rebecca Lowery, Associate Curator, with Emilia Nicholson-Fajardo, Curatorial Assistant, and Anastasia Kahn, former Curatorial Assistant, The Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles.

Josh Kline: Climate Change-MOCA.name: Josh Kline: Climate Change
Josh Kline: Climate Change-MOCA.description: Josh Kline’s Climate Change is both an exhibition and a total work of art—an ambitious, immersive suite of science-fiction installations that imagines a future sculpted by ruinous climate crisis and the ordinary people destined to inhabit it. Begun in 2018 and produced in sections over the last five years, Kline’s eponymous project will be brought together for the first time for this exhibition, mobilizing sculpture, moving image work, photography, and ephemeral materials to completely transform the galleries of MOCA Grand Avenue. Climate Change is a visceral, charged work of 21st-century expanded cinema. In this vision, which could be called dystopian but in truth is terrifyingly near, a catastrophic sea-level rise has inundated the world’s coasts, unleashing a flood of hundreds of millions traumatized refugees. What happens in a world where the systems built to sustain and extend capitalist enterprise and global hegemony melt down their own foundations? Kline opens the door to such a future, inviting us to place ourselves within it and consider the rear view. The exhibition is accompanied by a catalogue. This exhibition is carbon calculated. The museum reduced greenhouse gas emissions through planning efforts and balanced the remaining emissions through Strategic Climate Fund donations. Support provided by the MOCA Environmental Council. Josh Kline: Climate Change is organized by Rebecca Lowery, Associate Curator, with Emilia Nicholson-Fajardo, Curatorial Assistant, The Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles.

Reverberations-MOCA.name: Reverberations
Reverberations-MOCA.description: MOCA’s Collection, now numbering close to 8,000 works of art spanning the mid-20th century to the present, is internationally renowned for its depth and excellence across media, style, and art history. Highlighting areas of unique strength, these Collection galleries orient around single-artist presentations of work by Robert Rauschenberg and Mark Rothko and gather key acquisitions made by the museum throughout its forty-four-year history, including many selections from the foundational Panza, Schreiber, Weisman and Parsons Collections. Galleries devoted to abstraction, Pop, and conceptual work from the 1950s and 1960s are joined by recent acquisitions from Nairy Baghramian, Isa Genzken, and Rachel Harrison while figurative paintings by Michael Armitage, Jennifer Packer, and Henry Taylor join canonical works by Alice Neel, George Segal and others. Also on view are presentations of Robert Frank’s The Americans in its entirety and Renee Green’s installation Import-Export Funk Office (1993). Reverberations is organized by Bennett Simpson, Senior Curator, with Emilia Nicholson-Fajardo, Curatorial Assistant, The Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles.

Julian Charri\u00e8re: Deep End-MOCA.name: Julian Charrière: Deep End
Julian Charri\u00e8re: Deep End-MOCA.description: The works on view in Deep End explore the fragility and resilience of planetary water systems, engaging with the complexity of the sea not only as a regenerative carbon sink, habitat, chemical marker for climate change or liminal space, but also as a vast biogeological system in which we are entrenched. Presented therein are immersive environments and atmospheric conditions that evoke the ocean’s abyss, including a darkened exhibition space where multi-sensory experiences create a porous relationship between the viewer and object. Dreamlike compositions of moving image and sound bring audiences on a visceral journey into some of the planet’s most vulnerable and remote ecosystems, encouraging careful listening to the constant communication between the organisms that occupy it. Materials such as bitumen, ground coral, and mud from the deep seafloor are embedded in several works, becoming charged with human history and our impulse to transform the natural world into a resource. They mark an intersection between the accelerating consequences of anthropogenic environmental change and the slow geological time required to produce the carbon deposits that fuel it. A newly commissioned work, Hope Line (2026), features a live stream of a coral reef near Port Antonio, Jamaica, that was strongly affected by the 2023 El Niño bleaching event. This meditative installation allows visitors not only to witness and listen to one of the most important and biodiverse habitat types on the planet, but also to emit their own voices into it. Bridging time and place, Hope Line ultimately asks how art can act as a vector for advocacy. The exhibition also facilitates the beginning of a feasibility study for a closely related project titled Reefwards (2026), which combines underwater land art with coral reef restoration and conservation, developed through past and present collaboration with scientists, researchers, NGOs and advising universities, and most recently close dialogue with marine biologist and coral specialist Dr. Sebastian Schmidt-Roach and parametric designer and architect Phillipp Mecke. The exhibition will be accompanied by a catalogue. The Eric and Wendy Schmidt Environment and Art Prize is a juried award supporting artists whose practices engage critical intersections of art, architecture, design, climate, conservation, sustainability, and environmental justice. Julian Charrière: Deep End is organized by Paula Kroll, Assistant Curator, in collaboration with Kelsey Shell, Environmental & Sustainability Strategist, The Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles. Please be advised that one room in Julian Charrière: Deep End includes moving mirrored walls, a rotating light, and surround sound.

Cecilia Vicu\u00f1a The Dream of Water:.name: Cecilia Vicuña The Dream of Water: Quipu of Encounters Maricunga
Cecilia Vicu\u00f1a The Dream of Water:.description: The Dream of Water: Quipu of Encounters Maricunga is the latest in Vicuña’s series of collective actions developed with the participation of communities and publics in both museums and natural sites since the 1960s. The ecological crisis unfolding in the Salar de Maricunga, salt flats located in the southernmost part of the Atacama Desert in the high Andes is at the core of this exhibition. These ancient salt flats and lagoons, which form part of the ancestral territory of the Colla people, sustain extraordinary microbial communities and ecosystems that are increasingly threatened by corporate lithium mining and its heavy demands on the region’s scarce water resources. Suspended in MOCA’s tallest gallery, Parina Quipu (2026) is a textile sculpture made of unspun wool, sheared by artisans in southern Chile and naturally dyed in shades to evoke the landscape of Maricunga and the parinas, or Andean flamingos, whose nesting grounds are also being threatened. The adjacent gallery features Salar de Maricunga Quipu de Encuentro (2026), a five-channel video installation assembled from footage recorded during the artist’s journeys to Maricunga in December 2025 and May 2026. Moving from dusk to dawn across the Atacama landscape, the nonnarrative videos capture the region’s rich biodiversity while poetically documenting the rituals performed by the artist and her collaborators, including artists, scientists, musicians, filmmakers, activists, and Colla community members. Also playing in the gallery is Cosmo Sheldrake’s Canto de Maricunga (2026), a sound piece especially created for the quipu, weaving together field recordings, underwater sounds, and cosmic radio waves, alongside Vicuña’s chants and participants’ voices. On May 1, 2027, the artist will pesent a “living quipu” at MOCA, bringing together artists, activists, scientists, and water defenders from across the Los Angeles basin in a collective ritual. The Dream of Water: Quipu of Encounters Maricunga is organized by José Luis Blondet, Senior Curator, with Ariana Rizo, Curatorial Assistant, in collaboration with Kelsey Shell, Environmental & Sustainability Strategist, The Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles. This exhibition is accompanied by a publication. The Eric and Wendy Schmidt Environment and Art Prize is a juried award supporting artists whose practices engage critical intersections of art, architecture, design, climate, conservation, sustainability, and environmental justice.

Glenn Ligon: Sit So Your Back Isn't Agai.name: Glenn Ligon: Sit So Your Back Isn't Against The Door
Glenn Ligon: Sit So Your Back Isn't Agai.description: Glenn Ligon's Coloring Book paintings, made from children's markings on Afrocentric coloring books of the late 1960s and early 1970s, are on view together for the first time in over 25 years. The show also debuts a new 22-part work, 'Black Panther Coloring Book #1.' Opening reception Wed, Sep 30.

Jack Whitten: The Numinous-Hauser & Wirt.name: Jack Whitten: The Numinous
Jack Whitten: The Numinous-Hauser & Wirt.description: Paintings and works on paper from the 1980s, a decade of decisive experimentation in Jack Whitten's six-decade career, including the Soulspace paintings, circular acrylic reliefs, and Site paintings cast from urban textures. Opening reception Wed, Sep 30.

Night Window: David Smith Spray Painting.name: Night Window: David Smith Spray Paintings, 1958–1964
Night Window: David Smith Spray Painting.description: An exhibition devoted to David Smith's pioneering Sprays, seldom-seen two-dimensional works made by the sculptor at night, that show his daring innovations of form, color, space and time.

Making History: Manet\u2019s \u201cExecu.name: Making History: Manet’s “Execution of Maximilian” from the National Gallery, London
Making History: Manet\u2019s \u201cExecu.description: Édouard Manet’s The Execution of Maximilian (c. 1867–68) is one of the French artist’s most ambitious paintings, made all the more curious and compelling by its now-fragmentary condition. The second of five versions that Manet created of this violent 1867 event, the nearly life-size painting depicts the death by firing squad of the short-lived emperor of Mexico, Austrian archduke Ferdinand Maximilian, by forces serving ousted Mexican president Benito Juárez.

Takers | Makers: Photographic Practice i.name: Takers | Makers: Photographic Practice in California, 1945–1980

Raphael 2020-Norton Simon Museum.name: Raphael 2020
Raphael 2020-Norton Simon Museum.description: This winter and spring, the Norton Simon Museum joins institutions around the world in observing the 500th anniversary of Raphael’s death with a special display and a series of programs focused on the artist’sMadonna and Child with Book, from around 1502–3.

Unseen Picasso-Norton Simon Museum.name: Unseen Picasso
Unseen Picasso-Norton Simon Museum.description: Unseen Picassopresents a selection of innovative, rarely seen prints created throughout the artist’s prodigious career.

The Expressive Body: Memory, Devotion, D.name: The Expressive Body: Memory, Devotion, Desire (1400–1750)
The Expressive Body: Memory, Devotion, D.description: This exhibition explores the ways that images of the human body were used to generate profound physical and emotional responses in viewers throughout the 15th through 18th centuries.

Manet\u2019s Philosophers from the Art I.name: Manet’s Philosophers from the Art Institute of Chicago
Manet\u2019s Philosophers from the Art I.description: This special installation reunites three of Manet’sPhilosophersfor the first time in more than fifty years: The Norton Simon’sRagpicker, c. 1865–70, and two paintings on loan from the Art Institute,Beggar with Oysters (Philosopher)andBeggar with a Duffle Coat (Philosopher), both dated 1865/67.

Richard Hunt: Details-Norton Simon Museu.name: Richard Hunt: Details
Richard Hunt: Details-Norton Simon Museu.description: This focus exhibition features a selection of lithographs made by sculptor Richard Hunt during his 1965 residency at the Tamarind Lithography Workshop in Los Angeles.

Alternate Realities: Altoon, Diebenkorn,.name: Alternate Realities: Altoon, Diebenkorn, Lobdell, Woelffer
Alternate Realities: Altoon, Diebenkorn,.description: Drawn from the Norton Simon Museum’s expansive holdings of postwar American art,Alternate Realitiesexplores the ways in which artists John Altoon, Richard Diebenkorn, Frank Lobdell and Emerson Woelffer challenged the limitations of pure, gestural abstraction by exploiting the resonance of figural forms.

Modernism in Miniature-Norton Simon Muse.name: Modernism in Miniature
Modernism in Miniature-Norton Simon Muse.description: This intimate exhibition presents small-scale works of art by some of the most celebrated artists of the mid-20th century.

Ink, Paper, Stone: Six Women Artists and.name: Ink, Paper, Stone: Six Women Artists and the Language of Lithography
Ink, Paper, Stone: Six Women Artists and.description: This exhibition examines the prints of six critically acclaimed female artists who visited Los Angeles in the 1960s to explore the art of lithography: Ruth Asawa, Gego, Eleanore Mikus, Louise Nevelson, Irene Siegel and Hedda Sterne.

Picasso Ingres: Face to Face-Norton Simo.name: Picasso Ingres: Face to Face
Picasso Ingres: Face to Face-Norton Simo.description: In partnership with the National Gallery, London, this special installation brings together for the first time Pablo Picasso’s dazzlingWoman with a Bookwith the painting that inspired it, Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres’s late, great portraitMadame Moitessier(1856).

Saint Sebastian: Anatomy of a Sculpture-.name: Saint Sebastian: Anatomy of a Sculpture
Saint Sebastian: Anatomy of a Sculpture-.description: Through historical and scientific research, this small exhibition explores the rich life—from its creation to its arrival at the Museum—of a previously unstudied 15th-century Italian painted sculpture of St. Sebastian.

All Consuming: Art and the Essence of Fo.name: All Consuming: Art and the Essence of Food
All Consuming: Art and the Essence of Fo.description: This expansive exhibition explores how artists responded to and shaped food cultures in Europe from 1500 to 1900.

Word as Image-Norton Simon Museum.name: Word as Image
Word as Image-Norton Simon Museum.description: Spanning the comical to the political to the conceptual,Word as Imageexplores how artists challenge viewers to consider language and image anew, by positioning words as an essential part of visual culture.

Benevolent Beings: Buddhas and Bodhisatt.name: Benevolent Beings: Buddhas and Bodhisattvas from South and Southeast Asia
Benevolent Beings: Buddhas and Bodhisatt.description: Explore how buddhas, bodhisattvas and other protective deities have been seen to offer blessings, guidance and security to their devotees.

I Saw It: Francisco de Goya, Printmaker-.name: I Saw It: Francisco de Goya, Printmaker
I Saw It: Francisco de Goya, Printmaker-.description: This fascinating exhibition presents Spanish artist Francisco de Goya's four major print series in their entirety:Caprichos(1799),Desastres de la Guerra(c. 1810–15),La Tauromaquia(1815–16) andLos Disparates(c. 1815–23), offering insight into the artist's creative process and the full range of his expressive capacity.

I Saw It: Modern Artists Respond to Goya.name: I Saw It: Modern Artists Respond to Goya
I Saw It: Modern Artists Respond to Goya.description: On view in the Museum’s focus gallery, works by artists Enrique Chagoya, Leon Golub, Pablo Picasso, Yinka Shonibare and Andy Warhol demonstrate these artists’ deep connection with the concerns Goya expressed as a printmaker and even his direct influence on their art making.

Plugged In: Art and Electric Light-Norto.name: Plugged In: Art and Electric Light
Plugged In: Art and Electric Light-Norto.description: This illuminating exhibition shines a light on the ways that artists in the mid-20th century engaged with electric light in their artworks.

Look Alive! A Still Life Comparison-Nort.name: Look Alive! A Still Life Comparison
Look Alive! A Still Life Comparison-Nort.description: Explore the practice of slow looking through an intriguing pairing of two still-life paintings: Jacques Linard’sStill Life: The Five Senses with Flowers,1639, and Tom Wesselmann’sStill Life #2,1962.

Mariana: Vel\u00e1zquez\u2019s Portrait.name: Mariana: Velázquez’s Portrait of a Queen from the Museo Nacional del Prado
Mariana: Vel\u00e1zquez\u2019s Portrait.description: Exhibited on the West Coast for the very first time, Diego Velázquez’s extraordinary paintingQueen Mariana of Austria(1652–53) is on special loan from the Museo del Prado in Madrid.

Retrospect: 50 Years at the Norton Simon.name: Retrospect: 50 Years at the Norton Simon Museum
Retrospect: 50 Years at the Norton Simon.description: Through rare photos from the Museum’s archive,Retrospecthighlights both significant and lesser-known stories from the Museum’s 50-year history. This small exhibition is held in the Museum’s Focus Gallery.

Gold: Enduring Power, Sacred Craft-Norto.name: Gold: Enduring Power, Sacred Craft
Gold: Enduring Power, Sacred Craft-Norto.description: Organized on the occasion of the Museum’s 50th anniversary, a milestone traditionally associated with this metal,Gold: Enduring Power, Sacred Craftinvites fresh inquiry into the nature of gold as an artistic medium.

Dear Little Friend: Impressions of Galka.name: Dear Little Friend: Impressions of Galka Scheyer
Dear Little Friend: Impressions of Galka.description: This focus exhibition looks at the legacy of German-born art dealer Galka Scheyer, who played a pivotal role in bringing European modernism to the United States.

The Art of Kandy: Sri Lanka\u2019s Last.name: The Art of Kandy: Sri Lanka’s Last Kingdom
The Art of Kandy: Sri Lanka\u2019s Last.description: This focus exhibition features art from Kandy, the final royal capital of Sri Lanka before the onset of British colonial rule, that reflects wide-ranging themes of royal sponsorship, Buddhist devotion and creative imagination.

Second Nature: Interpreting Landscape-No.name: Second Nature: Interpreting Landscape
Second Nature: Interpreting Landscape-No.description: This focused exhibition explores how four distinctive artists visually interpreted the natural world. Jacob van Ruisdael, Gustave Courbet, Barbara Hepworth and Norman Zammitt are each represented by one of their works, all from the Norton Simon’s collections. While these objects—two paintings, one sculpture and one assemblage—belong to different eras, the ensemble inspires unexpected visual resonances that reveal how art can respond to and shape human relationships with the landscape.

Rembrandt\u2019s Spring: A Portrait of S.name: Rembrandt’s Spring: A Portrait of Saskia from the National Gallery, London
Rembrandt\u2019s Spring: A Portrait of S.description: The Norton Simon Museum presents a two-gallery exhibition centered on the loan of Rembrandt van Rijn’s painting Saskia van Uylenburgh in Arcadian Costume from the National Gallery, London, in which the artist depicts his wife, Saskia, as Flora, the Roman goddess of spring. Rembrandt created this painting in 1635, during a moment of new beginnings for the artist.

Laura Aguilar: Day of the Dead-Huntingto.name: Laura Aguilar: Day of the Dead
Laura Aguilar: Day of the Dead-Huntingto.description: Drawn from recent acquisitions from Laura Aguilar’s estate, “Laura Aguilar: Day of the Dead” presents photographs made from 1984 to 1992 documenting Día de los Muertos celebrations in Los Angeles.

Doyle Lane: Master of Clay-Huntington.name: Doyle Lane: Master of Clay
Doyle Lane: Master of Clay-Huntington.description: Experience the first major museum retrospective on Los Angeles ceramic artist Doyle Lane (1923–2002).

Stories from the Library: Damaged Goods-.name: Stories from the Library: Damaged Goods
Stories from the Library: Damaged Goods-.description: See how damaged objects, visible mistakes, and other imperfections reveal how physical traces can make library materials more compelling, beautiful, and revealing.

Stories from the Library: The Mirror of.name: Stories from the Library: The Mirror of the Moon
Stories from the Library: The Mirror of.description: Follow surprising threads across centuries that show how artists, scientists, writers, and dreamers have traced their ideas onto the lunar surface and discover how the moon is a mirror of humanity.

\"This Land Is ...\" Exhibition-Huntingt.name: "This Land Is ..." Exhibition
\"This Land Is ...\" Exhibition-Huntingt.description: In dialogue with the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, the exhibition brings together diverse perspectives on the relationship between nature and nation, and how the ideals of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness are intertwined with place.

Mercedes Dorame\u2014Deliquescence: Site.name: Mercedes Dorame—Deliquescence: Sites of Transformation
Mercedes Dorame\u2014Deliquescence: Site.description: Tongva artist Mercedes Dorame’s large-scale installation draws on archival research—including historical images of regional freshwater springs—to present her monumental photographs together with sculptural and painted elements. The installation reflects her ongoing interest in place, memory, and the presence of ancestral histories.

Sandy Rodriguez: Book 13-Huntington.name: Sandy Rodriguez: Book 13
Sandy Rodriguez: Book 13-Huntington.description: Sandy Rodriguez’s “Book 13,” her largest installation to date, includes a 20-foot-wide map of the United States, plant portraits, a book, and a landscape painting, all created on hand-processed amate-fiber paper. Drawing on a range of colonial Mexican sources in dialogue with 19th-century maps and boundary surveys from The Huntington’s collections, the installation brings together research on place, ecology, and regional histories.

the eight directions of the wind: Edmund.name: the eight directions of the wind: Edmund de Waal at The Huntington
the eight directions of the wind: Edmund.description: The Huntington presents the evocative works of acclaimed British artist and author Edmund de Waal in “the eight directions of the wind: Edmund de Waal at The Huntington.” This yearlong exhibition features de Waal’s site-specific installations at three iconic Huntington sites: the Huntington Art Gallery, the Chinese Garden, and the Japanese Garden.

Mineo Mizuno: Homage to Nature-Huntingto.name: Mineo Mizuno: Homage to Nature
Mineo Mizuno: Homage to Nature-Huntingto.description: This site-specific work explores the fragility of the Earth’s ecosystem, as well as the destruction of the forest and its potential for regeneration. The sculpture celebrates the beauty of wood in its natural state and emphasizes its potential as a reusable and renewable resource.

Betye Saar: Drifting Toward Twilight-Hun.name: Betye Saar: Drifting Toward Twilight
Betye Saar: Drifting Toward Twilight-Hun.description: Renowned American artist Betye Saar’s large-scale work “Drifting Toward Twilight”—commissioned by The Huntington—is a site-specific installation that features a 17-foot-long vintage wooden canoe and found objects, including birdcages, antlers, and natural materials harvested by Saar from The Huntington’s grounds.

Reimagined American Art Galleries-Huntin.name: Reimagined American Art Galleries
Reimagined American Art Galleries-Huntin.description: Discover seven newly unveiled galleries of American art.

Mapel Orientation Gallery-Huntington.name: Mapel Orientation Gallery
Mapel Orientation Gallery-Huntington.description: Learn about the founding of The Huntington, grab a themed tour guide, and even create your own masterpiece!

Borderlands-Huntington.name: Borderlands
Borderlands-Huntington.description: See artwork from the 19th century to today in dialogue with installations by contemporary artists that offer fresh perspectives on American art.

Red Earth by Lita Albuquerque-Huntington.name: Red Earth by Lita Albuquerque
Red Earth by Lita Albuquerque-Huntington.description: Installed near the southern entrance to the Japanese Garden, Lita Albuquerque’s Red Earth features an approximately 6-by-4-foot rock slab coated with bright red pigment and surrounded by bamboo.

Petromania: Obsessing About Stones in As.name: Petromania: Obsessing About Stones in Asia and America
Petromania: Obsessing About Stones in As.description: Discover how extraordinary stones became objects of art, imagination, and contemplation across China, Japan, and the United States.

Robert Indiana\u2019s \u2018LOVE\u2019 a.name: Robert Indiana’s ‘LOVE’ at The Huntington
Robert Indiana\u2019s \u2018LOVE\u2019 a.description: Robert Indiana’s monumental LOVE —one of the most recognizable works of postwar American art—has joined The Huntington’s permanent collection. Robert Indiana first conceived LOVE as a drawing in 1964. The image appeared on the Museum of Modern Art’s annual holiday card the following year, and the first LOVE sculpture debuted in New York City in May 1966. With its stacked letters and distinctive tilted “O,” the composition soon became a defining image of Pop Art.

Inventing America: The Comic Book Revolu.name: Inventing America: The Comic Book Revolution
Inventing America: The Comic Book Revolu.description: Explore the United States in the twentieth century through the lens of the American art form: the comic book. Inventing America: The Comic Book Revolution examines how this art form became a revolutionary cultural medium, shaping national identity through distinctive stories and characters.

The 1960s\u2014A Generation on Fire: Jud.name: The 1960s—A Generation on Fire: Judy Baca's Great Wall of Los Angeles

Jenny Yurshansky: What We Carry-Skirball.name: Jenny Yurshansky: What We Carry
Jenny Yurshansky: What We Carry-Skirball.description: Skirball Artist in Residence Jenny Yurshansky explores how memories and family history shape our sense of home and belonging through collected objects and LA immigration stories.

Patrisse Cullors: Wishes Made Material-S.name: Patrisse Cullors: Wishes Made Material
Patrisse Cullors: Wishes Made Material-S.description: Artist and activist Patrisse Cullors debuts three new works inspired by a series of Black and Jewish dialogues at the Skirball, asking what becomes possible when we move toward one another rather than away, and when the histories we carry are held not in isolation, but in company.

Common Ground-Skirball Cultural Center.name: Common Ground
Common Ground-Skirball Cultural Center.description: Los Angeles–based artist Adam Silverman collected clay, water, and wood ash from all fifty American states, Washington DC, and the five inhabited US Territories and combined them to create a set of tableware and ceremonial pots. The resulting 224 ceramic objects, titled Common Ground, is a community-activated artwork that celebrates American pluralism while also fostering human connection through shared meals and collaborative installations.

Paul R. Williams: An Architect Considere.name: Paul R. Williams: An Architect Considered

Uhengaparaoa, Taonga Tuku Iho: Ancestral.name: Uhengaparaoa, Taonga Tuku Iho: Ancestral Gifts and Contemporary Māori Art
Uhengaparaoa, Taonga Tuku Iho: Ancestral.description: Inspired by the legacy of Uhengaparaoa, a renowned Whakatōhea weaver who traveled to the East Coast of Aotearoa New Zealand to share her weaving knowledge, Uhengaparaoa, Taonga Tuku Iho brings ancient and modern Māori art into dialogue.

Field Notes from Begumpura-Fowler Museum.name: Field Notes from Begumpura
Field Notes from Begumpura-Fowler Museum.description: Field Notes from Begumpura is an ongoing project by artist Rahee Punyashloka that imagines a future where Dalit and Adivasi communities live free from the violence and oppression of the caste system. Inspired by the 15th-century poem “Begumpura” (“The City with No Sorrows”) by Guru Ravidas—one of South Asia’s earliest visions of a utopian society—the project takes the form of speculative ethnographic field notes documenting this fictional casteless world.

Textiles as Monument-Fowler Museum at UC.name: Textiles as Monument
Textiles as Monument-Fowler Museum at UC.description: What constitutes a monument, and who is memorialized? Three contemporary artists of South Asian descent—Suchitra Mattai, Jagdeep Raina, and Swapnaa Tamhane—transform textiles of their cultural heritage into memorials for those who have been unrecognized in public displays of historical memory. These artworks question why monuments are made and who is given the power to be remembered.

Mountain Spirits: Rice and Indigeneity i.name: Mountain Spirits: Rice and Indigeneity in the Northern Luzon Highlands, Philippines
Mountain Spirits: Rice and Indigeneity i.description: For generations, the Ifugao of northern Luzon have transformed steep mountainsides into rice terraces—astonishing feats of engineering that are also sacred landscapes shaped by ritual, community, and a profound connection to land.

Anida Yoeu Ali: The Buddhist Bug-Vincent.name: Anida Yoeu Ali: The Buddhist Bug
Anida Yoeu Ali: The Buddhist Bug-Vincent.description: Anida Yoeu Ali’s The Buddhist Bug is an expansive performance project that brings together myth, humor, spiritual inquiry, and the lived experience of displacement. At its center is a monumental saffron-colored creature, nearly 328 feet in length, with a human face tightly framed in cloth at one end and a pair of feet at the other.

francis and anthony almend\u00e1rez: nav.name: francis and anthony almendárez: navigating the archives within, vol. 2
francis and anthony almend\u00e1rez: nav.description: In their ongoing film and performance series Navigating the Archives Within, artists Francis and Anthony Almendárez examine how Latinx communities are represented and misrepresented across American film, television, music, and digital media. Developed from their vantage point as brothers whose family roots span Central America and the United States, they use sound and place to illuminate the broader forces that inform individual and collective identity.

California Collectives: Asian American m.name: California Collectives: Asian American moderns, 1924-1965
California Collectives: Asian American m.description: California Collectives: Asian American Moderns, 1924-1965 features more than fifty paintings, drawings, watercolors, prints, and photographs by American artists of Asian descent.

New Voices: The 2027 District Wide Stude.name: New Voices: The 2027 District Wide Student Art Biennial
New Voices: The 2027 District Wide Stude.description: The 2027 District Wide Student Art Biennial spotlights works created by students between the Spring 2025 and Fall 2026 semesters.

Nurtured Flames: The Medicine of Fire-Ar.name: Nurtured Flames: The Medicine of Fire

NOMAD: Dominique Moody and the Assemblag.name: NOMAD: Dominique Moody and the Assemblage of Home

Pictures of Belonging: Miki Hayakawa, Hi.name: Pictures of Belonging: Miki Hayakawa, Hisako Hibi, and Miné Okubo

Momo Nagano: Archeology of Motherhood-18.name: Momo Nagano: Archeology of Motherhood
Momo Nagano: Archeology of Motherhood-18.description: Recently discovered bundled in storage under Nagano’s Silverlake home, these weavings were components of a larger installation piece displayed in the “Magical Mystery Tour” exhibition at Municipal Art Gallery in Barnsdall Art Park in 1978. It is believed that Nagano had begun to deconstruct the piece before putting it in storage almost half a century ago. Here, it has been improvisationally re-assembled by her son.

Haruka Yamada: \u201cSun of the City\u20.name: Haruka Yamada: “Sun of the City” Mural
Haruka Yamada: \u201cSun of the City\u20.description: During Haruka Yamada’s three month stay at 18th Street Arts Center from Tokyo, Japan as part of the Call to Dream: The Sam Francis Fellowship, she created “Sun of the City”. It is a project that utilizes existing constructions to create site-specific sundials that function uniquely in each location. Through this project, Yamada aim to reconsider the rules and systems of time and timekeeping, which we often unconsciously perceive as correct but historically have also served as symbols of power.

Lauren Bon: Meandros-18th Street Arts Ce.name: Lauren Bon: Meandros
Lauren Bon: Meandros-18th Street Arts Ce.description: 18th Street Arts Center is proud to announce a new site-specific permanent public artwork by Lauren Bon and Metabolic Studio. This work invites collective reflection and dialogue on how cities can reconnect with natural systems, particularly the rainwater cycle, to create resilience in the face of environmental and urban challenges.

Rhizome\u2019s Solar Server-18th Street.name: Rhizome’s Solar Server
Rhizome\u2019s Solar Server-18th Street.description: 18th Street Arts Center is excited to partner with Rhizome on the launch of their new solar server, which is installed on the roof of 18th Street. Solar Protocol is a global web platform hosted across a network of solar-powered servers stewarded by artists and volunteers around the world. Each server—powered only by a small solar panel and battery—offers intermittent connectivity that shifts with available sunlight, weather, and season.

Hilla Toony Navok: Yellow Marquee-18th S.name: Hilla Toony Navok: Yellow Marquee
Hilla Toony Navok: Yellow Marquee-18th S.description: A small yellow awning appears to have slipped from the wall and settled almost on the ground. Losing its purpose as a protector from the sun, it becomes a small autonomous space that suggests both shelter and isolation.

RED ALL NIGHTmare on 18th Street \u2013.name: RED ALL NIGHTmare on 18th Street – Opening Reception

Ghost Agency: Smooth Criminal-18th Stree.name: Ghost Agency: Smooth Criminal
Ghost Agency: Smooth Criminal-18th Stree.description: Smooth Criminal reimagines public sculpture for an era shaped by digital networks, surveillance, and questions of personal agency. Developed by Ghost Agency (Gro Sarauw and Anni Garza Lau), the project moves beyond traditional notions of monumentality and permanence, proposing instead a distributed sculptural system that exists across both physical and digital space.

Molly Cleator and Anne Bray present: Ski.name: Molly Cleator and Anne Bray present: Skirting
Molly Cleator and Anne Bray present: Ski.description: Over three to four weeks, Molly Cleator and Anne Bray will be in residence to develop a room of installations combining video projections and monitors, sculptural elements, figures, sound tracks, spoken word and the space under two skirts. The outcome will be presented over the final weekend of April 24-25, 2027: Friday and Saturday night viewings with an afternoon of dialogue and snacks.

The Final Rally: Anemone Bleaching-18th.name: The Final Rally: Anemone Bleaching
The Final Rally: Anemone Bleaching-18th.description: The Final Rally: Anemone Bleaching Solo Exhibition by Xingyu Huang “‘Symbiosis’ was born in biology. The word began its journey into the common lexicon in 1887, when lichenologists attempted to describe the field condition of “with-living”-life found exist-ing with other life on Earth.

Gateway to Himalayan Art-USC Pacific Asi.name: Gateway to Himalayan Art
Gateway to Himalayan Art-USC Pacific Asi.description: Gateway to Himalayan Art introduces the main forms, concepts, meanings, and religious traditions of Himalayan art with objects from the collection of the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, New York.

We Are Connected: Highlights from the US.name: We Are Connected: Highlights from the USC Pacific Asia Museum Himalayan Collection
We Are Connected: Highlights from the US.description: We live in a world teeming with beings, things, and forces of all sorts. We Are Connected offers you an opportunity to explore the various ways in which inhabitants of the Tibetan Plateau, the Himalayas, and Inner Asia relate to each other as well as to the animals, plants, mountains, and spirits around them through art and material culture.

Hung Liu: Secret Freedom-USC Pacific Asi.name: Hung Liu: Secret Freedom
Hung Liu: Secret Freedom-USC Pacific Asi.description: Groundbreaking Chinese American artist Hung Liu (1948–2021) came of age under Mao Zedong’s Cultural Revolution, when artistic expression was tightly controlled and painting outside official doctrine carried real risk.

Ten Years to Sharpen a Sword: Lauren YS.name: Ten Years to Sharpen a Sword: Lauren YS Featuring Makoto
Ten Years to Sharpen a Sword: Lauren YS.description: Ten Years to Sharpen a Sword marks the first solo museum exhibition by internationally recognized artist Lauren YS, whose vibrant, high-energy murals and paintings create immersive worlds where ancestral memory and queer embodiments intertwine, often with hybrid beings that are part creature and inspired by East Asian mythology.

Bumdog Torres-Wende Museum.name: Bumdog Torres
Bumdog Torres-Wende Museum.description: In THIS STRUCTURE WILL BE REMOVED WITHIN THE NEXT 48 HOURS, Los Angeles artist Bumdog Torres looks at the beautiful, organic, and tragically short-lived attachments people form to their possessions and the places they live. The installation opens in the guardhouse on Saturday, November 7, alongside Competing Cosmologies: Interpreting the Sky.

Between Two Empires: Argentina in the Co.name: Between Two Empires: Argentina in the Cold War Pendulum (1945–1989)
Between Two Empires: Argentina in the Co.description: Photographs from the archives of the newspapers La Razón and Clarín trace four decades of Argentine political life, from Perón to the return of democracy. Press photographers recorded rallies, coups, and daily life as the country swung between competing powers, and their images show how ideology shapes what a nation sees of itself.

Competing Cosmologies: Interpreting the.name: Competing Cosmologies: Interpreting the Sky
Competing Cosmologies: Interpreting the.description: Co-curated by the Wende’s Curatorial Department and NASA historian Lois Rosson, Competing Cosmologies explores how new discoveries in space exploration during and after the Cold War have inspired visual artists around the world.

Carlos Castro Arias: Vandalismo Artesana.name: Carlos Castro Arias: Vandalismo Artesanal
Carlos Castro Arias: Vandalismo Artesana.description: Colombian artist Carlos Castro Arias’s first solo exhibition in Los Angeles explores perspectival histories of the conquest of the Americas through the use of opposing craft traditions: bronze casting—a European technique long associated with monuments to colonial power—set against weaving with natural fibers, beads, and ancestral materials that carry the knowledge of Indigenous peoples and belief systems.

Embers of Generational Memory-Craft Cont.name: Embers of Generational Memory
Embers of Generational Memory-Craft Cont.description: For more than 35 years, the California Community Foundation’s Fellowship for Visual Artists (FVA) has provided financial support and professional resources to more than 300 visual artists in Los Angeles County. This exhibition highlights the 2026-2027 FVA cohort—a dedicated group of artists whose practices reflect the histories, cultures, and geographies of Los Angeles.

Maker-in-Residence: Meztli Projects-Craf.name: Maker-in-Residence: Meztli Projects
Maker-in-Residence: Meztli Projects-Craf.description: Meztli Projects is a collective of contemporary Indigenous artists that promotes the creative development of Native and Indigenous Peoples by providing an ecosystem that reconnects generations, supports cultural production, and contributes to knowledge building and transmission.

B\u2019atz\u2019: Legacy in Guatemalan T.name: B’atz’: Legacy in Guatemalan Textiles & Contemporary Art
B\u2019atz\u2019: Legacy in Guatemalan T.description: Named for B’atz’, the Maya day sign associated with the thread of life, weaving, creativity, knowledge, and the beginning of time, B’atz’: Legacy in Guatemalan Textiles & Contemporary Art is a major exhibition and research initiative that explores the enduring vitality of Maya textile traditions and their influence on contemporary artistic practice in Guatemala.

Sadie Barnette: How to Fly-California Af.name: Sadie Barnette: How to Fly
Sadie Barnette: How to Fly-California Af.description: How to Fly is a site-specific photomural by visual artist Sadie Barnette installed in CAAM’s atrium. Born and raised in Oakland, California, Barnette incorporates photographs she has taken of locations across the state with pictures from her family archives. The installation includes references to Barnette’s past artworks, as well as her signature motifs, such as glitter, rhinestones, cars, and plant life.

Free and Queer: Black Californian Roots.name: Free and Queer: Black Californian Roots of Gay Liberation
Free and Queer: Black Californian Roots.description: Free and Queer: Black Californian Roots of Gay Liberation presents California as a pioneering site of sustained, Black-led struggles for LGBTQ equality, civil rights, and recognition. The exhibition recovers histories largely excluded from existing narratives and exposes powerful ways that print culture, artistic practice, and performance styles shaped, advanced, and interpreted Black queer social movements alongside political and legal activism.

Reggie Burrows Hodges: A Theater of Mira.name: Reggie Burrows Hodges: A Theater of Miracles
Reggie Burrows Hodges: A Theater of Mira.description: Reggie Burrows Hodges (b. 1965, Compton) is known for his sensuous black and jewel-toned paintings of labor, community rituals, and solitary moments. His paintings combine observations of contemporary life with traditional artist techniques that date back centuries to the Renaissance era.

Sinners: Sounds That Summon-California A.name: Sinners: Sounds That Summon
Sinners: Sounds That Summon-California A.description: Sound has the power to form creative worlds that manifest joy, protection, belonging, and freedom. Sinners: Sounds That Summon revisits the fan-favorite Club Juke sequence in Ryan Coogler and Proximity Media’s 2025 film, Sinners, from Warner Bros. Pictures, in which music acts as a portal through time, from traditional African ritual to present-day street dance.

Fred Wilson: Reflections-California Afri.name: Fred Wilson: Reflections
Fred Wilson: Reflections-California Afri.description: Working across a range of media, spanning sculpture, photography, installation, and painting, Fred Wilson (b. 1954, Bronx, New York) is best known for his conceptual interventions that expose the ways museums, archives, and institutions shape our understanding of the past. By reframing cultural narratives and recontextualizing objects, Wilson shifts perspectives to reveal structural inequalities and overlooked contributions of marginalized people, particularly Black communities worldwide.

Jamea Richmond-Edwards: Another World an.name: Jamea Richmond-Edwards: Another World and Yet the Same
Jamea Richmond-Edwards: Another World an.description: Another World and Yet the Same is Detroit-based artist Jamea Richmond-Edwards’s first solo exhibition in Los Angeles. It features new works alongside a selection of vibrant multimedia paintings from the last seven years that illustrate her rich, interdisciplinary practice.

Concrete Forms: A Look at the Brillembou.name: Concrete Forms: A Look at the Brillembourg-Capriles Collection
Concrete Forms: A Look at the Brillembou.description: The Museum of Latin American Art is pleased to present, for the first time in its galleries, a selection from the prestigious Tanya Brillembourg Capriles Collection.

Sigils: Unveiling the Sacred in the MOLA.name: Sigils: Unveiling the Sacred in the MOLAA Permanent Collection
Sigils: Unveiling the Sacred in the MOLA.description: To celebrate MOLAA’s 30th anniversary, this exhibition highlights artworks from the Permanent Collection that explore the diverse spiritual traditions that enrich the cultures of Latin America and the Caribbean. From the religious presence of Christianity, Judaism, and Santería, to the esoteric mysticism of the occult, these practices aim to connect to something beyond the natural world.

RED RED RED, Geometry of a Scar-Museum o.name: RED RED RED, Geometry of a Scar
RED RED RED, Geometry of a Scar-Museum o.description: The Museum of Latin American Art (MOLAA) announces the opening of RED, RED, RED, Geometry of a Scar, an international exhibition dedicated to women artists, organized by MIA Art Collection and curated by guest curator Sebastian C. Strenger. The exhibition brings together unique works by artists from around the world and explores the color red as a powerful visual, emotional, and symbolic thread connecting women artists.

Antonio Romero: TROPICALIA [VOL2]-Museum.name: Antonio Romero: TROPICALIA [VOL2]
Antonio Romero: TROPICALIA [VOL2]-Museum.description: The Museum of Latin American Art is pleased to present the first solo exhibition in the United States of Salvadoran artist Antonio Romero, whose works are part of the collections of MOLAA and the Museo Reina Sofía in Spain.

Carl Cheng: Nature Never Loses-Institute.name: Carl Cheng: Nature Never Loses
Carl Cheng: Nature Never Loses-Institute.venue: Institute of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles
Carl Cheng: Nature Never Loses-Institute.description: A landmark retrospective, Carl Cheng: Nature Never Loses is the first in-depth survey of the six-decade career of a pioneering Los Angeles artist whose genre-defying work explores environmental change and the role of technology in society. An overdue and deserving examination of his wide-ranging accomplishments, the exhibition brings together approximately 50 rarely exhibited artworks and archival ephemera and is accompanied by a comprehensive catalogue.

Zoe Walsh: Gathering-Institute of Contem.name: Zoe Walsh: Gathering
Zoe Walsh: Gathering-Institute of Contem.venue: Institute of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles
Zoe Walsh: Gathering-Institute of Contem.description: As a painter, Zoe Walsh (b. 1989, Washington, DC; lives and works in Los Angeles) refuses and expands the bounds of their chosen medium, disrupting the conventions of canvas and paint; bending figure and ground; entwining deep research and embodied practice. Walsh engages a range of disciplines with curiosity and care, from trans visual studies to urban planning to poetry.

Amia Yokoyama: Our Strange Hollows-Insti.name: Amia Yokoyama: Our Strange Hollows
Amia Yokoyama: Our Strange Hollows-Insti.venue: Institute of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles
Amia Yokoyama: Our Strange Hollows-Insti.description: A fissure is a break, an opening, a threshold, and a throughway–a vent through which we slip through the cracks from this world to the next. Mythology functions in a similar way, enabling us to break open our sense of the universe and to enter, even if only temporarily, into the volcanic voids and the heavenly hollows of beyond.

Teresa Baker: Somewhere Between Earth an.name: Teresa Baker: Somewhere Between Earth and Sky
Teresa Baker: Somewhere Between Earth an.venue: Institute of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles
Teresa Baker: Somewhere Between Earth an.description: In spring 2027, ICA LA will present Teresa Baker: Somewhere Between Earth and Sky. The most comprehensive presentation of Baker’s work to date, the exhibition will feature works made over the last decade—including a newly commissioned mural as well as a selection of over two dozen paintings, recent sculptures, and a suite of rarely exhibited drawings—that illuminate the artist’s persistent investigations into shape, color, line, and the natural world.

Sming Sming Books: LONG LIVE BOOKS!-Inst.name: Sming Sming Books: LONG LIVE BOOKS!
Sming Sming Books: LONG LIVE BOOKS!-Inst.venue: Institute of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles
Sming Sming Books: LONG LIVE BOOKS!-Inst.description: Presented in conjunction with ICA LA’s Bookshelf Residency with Sming Sming Books, LONG LIVE BOOKS! is a salon-style installation of papercuts created by artist Kate Laster with texts by Vivian Sming, Bay Area-based artist and Sming Sming Books founder.

Chris Martin: In Memory of My Feelings-D.name: Chris Martin: In Memory of My Feelings
Chris Martin: In Memory of My Feelings-D.description: David Kordansky Gallery is pleased to present In Memory of My Feelings, an exhibition of recent paintings by Chris Martin. The exhibition is on view in Los Angeles at 5130 W. Edgewood Pl. from November 13 through December 16, 2026. An opening reception will be held on Friday, November 13 from 6 to 8 PM.

Ivan Morley: Trees-David Kordansky Galle.name: Ivan Morley: Trees
Ivan Morley: Trees-David Kordansky Galle.description: David Kordansky Gallery is pleased to present Trees, a solo exhibition of new paintings by Ivan Morley. The exhibition is on view in Los Angeles at 5130 W. Edgewood Pl. from November 13 through December 16, 2026. An opening reception will be held on Friday, November 13, 2026, from 6 – 8 PM.

Abraham Lincoln Walker: After World, 198.name: Abraham Lincoln Walker: After World, 1980–1991
Abraham Lincoln Walker: After World, 198.description: David Kordansky Gallery is pleased to present Abraham Lincoln Walker: After World, 1980–1991, the gallery’s first solo exhibition of paintings by Abraham Lincoln Walker (b. 1921, d. 1993), a visionary self-taught American artist whose extraordinary output was largely unknown during his lifetime. The exhibition will be on view in Los Angeles at 5130 W. Edgewood Pl. from November 13 – December 16, 2026. An opening reception will be held on Friday, November 13, from 6 to 8 PM.

Wendy Red Star: False Stars-Roberts Proj.name: Wendy Red Star: False Stars
Wendy Red Star: False Stars-Roberts Proj.description: Roberts Projects is pleased to present False Stars, an exhibition of new work by Wendy Red Star that takes the Star Quilt through a series of material transformations. Named for the scientific phenomenon whereby a celestial formation is wrongly assumed to be a full-fledged star, the exhibition brings together mirrored installations and works on paper that show the enduring symbolic resonance of the stars.

Collins Obijiaku: Wherever You Are, Reme.name: Collins Obijiaku: Wherever You Are, Remember Me
Collins Obijiaku: Wherever You Are, Reme.description: Roberts Projects is pleased to present Wherever You Are, Remember Me, an exhibition of new works by Collins Obijiaku and the artist’s third solo presentation with the gallery. Bringing together portraits and still lifes rendered in his distinctive linework and graphic compositions, the exhibition emerges from Obijiaku’s recent relocation from his native Nigeria to Chicago.

Kuldeep Singh-Nazarian / Curcio.name: Kuldeep Singh
Kuldeep Singh-Nazarian / Curcio.description: Nazarian / Curcio is pleased to present Neither Sun nor Moon, a solo exhibition of new paintings by Brooklyn-based artist Kuldeep Singh, marking his debut with the gallery. Bringing together nine new works, the exhibition features portraits of male figures in quiet, contemplative moments, exploring intimacy, desire, and longing...

Mar Figueroa-Nazarian / Curcio.name: Mar Figueroa
Mar Figueroa-Nazarian / Curcio.description: Nazarian / Curcio is pleased to present The Witching Hour, a solo exhibition of new work by artist Mar Figueroa. Bringing together five works, including paintings incorporating handmade ceramic elements, the exhibition explores the relationship between the natural and spiritual worlds, drawing on the artist’s upbringing in an Ecuadorian...

Peter McRury-Nazarian / Curcio.name: Peter McRury
Peter McRury-Nazarian / Curcio.description: Nazarian / Curcio is pleased to present At a Familiar Distance, a solo exhibition of new paintings by Peter McRury, marking his debut with the gallery and his first solo exhibition in Los Angeles. Bringing together seven paintings, the exhibition draws on the familiar genres of portraiture, still life,...

Farah Al Qasimi-Fran\u00e7ois Ghebaly.name: Farah Al Qasimi
Farah Al Qasimi-Fran\u00e7ois Ghebaly.description: François Ghebaly is proud to present Rubberneck, Farah Al Qasimi’s second solo exhibition at the gallery and first presentation at the Beverly Hills location. Rubberneck opens ahead of Al Qasimi’s forthcoming institutional solo exhibition at the Whitney Museum of American Art in January 2027. Farah Al Qasimi creates films,...

Rigoberto Torres: Vecinos-Charlie James.name: Rigoberto Torres: Vecinos
Rigoberto Torres: Vecinos-Charlie James.description: Charlie James Gallery is pleased to present Vecinos, an exhibition by the iconic sculptor Rigoberto Torres. The works on view span over forty years and encompass a range of figures and sizes that together capture the artist’s vibrant and evolving Bronx community.

Jay Bell: Reason to Believe-Charlie Jame.name: Jay Bell: Reason to Believe
Jay Bell: Reason to Believe-Charlie Jame.description: Charlie James Gallery is pleased to present Jay Bell: Reason to Believe, an exhibition of new paintings by the Encinitas-based artist. Working directly from photos taken in his travels around California, Mexico and beyond, Bell paints portraits of communities by capturing the vehicles that carry them.

James McClung: At That Moment-Charlie Ja.name: James McClung: At That Moment
James McClung: At That Moment-Charlie Ja.description: Charlie James Gallery is pleased to present James McClung: At That Moment, the Inland Empire-based artist’s first exhibition with the gallery. McClung’s diaristic paintings capture moments in time with a keen eye toward framing and detail, inviting the viewer to consider the small occasions, chance encounters, and fleeting serendipities that fill the days, if one’s eyes are open to them. Many of the works on view capture moments of transition.

Erin Wright: Memnosphere-Anat Ebgi Galle.name: Erin Wright: Memnosphere
Erin Wright: Memnosphere-Anat Ebgi Galle.description: LOS ANGELES—Anat Ebgi is pleased to present the gallery’s second solo exhibition with Los Angeles-based artist and architect Erin Wright. The exhibition, entitled Memnosphere, is on view at 6150 Wilshire Blvd from September 19 through January 16. An opening reception will be held with the artist on Saturday, September 19, 6-8 pm. Jenny Morgan: Hours at the Edge-Anat Ebg.description: LOS ANGELES—Anat Ebgi is pleased to present new oil paintings by New York-based artist Jenny Morgan. The exhibition entitled Hours at the Edge is Morgan’s second solo exhibition with the gallery and debut presentation in Los Angeles. On view at 6150 Wilshire Blvd from November 13 – January 16. Jemima Wyman: Shimmering Menace-Commonwe.description: Commonwealth and Council presents Shimmering Menace, an exhibition of new work by Jemima Wyman. Since 2008, Wyman has built an extensive perso...

Maryrose Cobarrubias Mendoza: AAAgent pr.description: AAAgent presents Past Time, a multi-dimensional installation by Maryrose Cobarrubias Mendoza behind a succession of three doors along the corr...

Richard Avedon: Hollywood-Gagosian Bever.name: Richard Avedon: Hollywood
Richard Avedon: Hollywood-Gagosian Bever.description: Gagosian is pleased to present Richard Avedon: Hollywood, an exhibition of more than 120 photographs spanning Avedon’s career of over half a century and including some of his most iconic portraits alongside rarely seen images. The exhibition represents Hollywood as a profoundly American construct whose glamour and power have made it a global cultural touchstone. Opening at the Beverly Hills gallery on November 4, 2026, the presentation is curated by the Richard Avedon Foundation.

Jeffrey Deitch and Pace Gallery will present Untethered Journey, an exhibition of historical and recent works by Kiki Smith, at Deitch’s gallery at 925 N Orange Drive in Los Angeles from October 30, 2026, through January 23, 2027.
